body: Seems like we need a new mixin to me, as the set isn't really the same. There may be a separate question as to whether you want to also add IDL attributes for origin, protocol, host, hostname, etc., but even then reusing HTMLHyperlinkElementUtils wouldn't really work because it has a definition for href you don't want.
Could add a note that SVG elements use a different href definition?
No, mixins do not operate on the basis of notes.
We already include HTMLHyperlinkElementUtils but I think that is a mistake as no one implements it and part of the problem is it includes href as you say.
I wonder if a shared mixin makes sense given that SVG elements don't need [CEReactions] as far as I know. Shared definitions might make sense though, depending on the specifics.

The [CEReactions] bit is interesting--it seems we've taken a pretty substantial design decision to exclude any other types of elements besides HTML elements (the `ElementDefinitionOptions:extends` only looks for HTML Namespace'd names, class constructors must only extend `HTMLElement`, etc.). I'm a little hesitant to suggest this restriction be lifted for the sake of convergence (though extending SVG Polygon to make a Star element would be cool--our implementation uses a common base element class which would make this trivial).

Is there a short-term solution here? Could we make [CEReactions] be a no-op for APIs whose interfaces are not derived through HTMLElement? Or if a mixin is simply out-of-the-question, I guess perhaps the SVG spec could directly reference API definitions in HTML...?

The reason I prefer a mixin if we can get around the [CEReactions] issue is that HTML and SVG move at their own pace. Currently they're out of sync with each other, such as HTML having `ping` while SVG doesn't. Having them in a mixin allows SVG to inherit the new members that make sense for both when HTML inevitably progresses. There have already been cases of that before HTMLorSVGElement became a thing, as focus() added a parameter in HTML but still retained the old signature in SVG (technically it still does until the PR with the new syntax merges and I can make that update to link to WhatWG HTML mixins)

I don't think CEReactions is a big deal. I think it's already a no-op when used on properties which wouldn't trigger custom element reactions. It might make implementations a bit slower though if they just used that IDL directly (they'd do a few custom elements-related steps which are always pointless in the SVG case). I guess that's fixable with a slightly smarter bindings generator though.

HTMLHyperlinkElementUtils is a bigger issue. It sounds like that may need to be split up if SVG wants to reuse it.
Splitting up HTMLHyperlinkElementUtils isn't much of an issue though, other than some editorial hassle?
Yeah, I meant bigger as in "is currently very broken in the SVG spec". The fix is pretty small.

If we include a mixin should we include ping, referrerPolicy and text? Those are the three that are currently not defined on SVGAElement. I suppose if relList.supports() is useful on anchors for noopener and norefferer then at least referrerPolicy is useful. Ping is probably useful too.

I think it would make sense that if we want more shared code and a more unified interface for hyperlinks we should share as much as possible. 😊

Now this does also depend somewhat on the willingness of implementers to support all these and someone writing tests (ideally making the tests for `<a>` and `<area>` more generic).

Yeah. I've been putting tests in SVG as my plan was to test the current SVG2 (tests were not written as the features were added to the spec ) but I can add to the HTML tests if that makes it easier.

For browser support, Firefox already supports download (using DOMString) but not the others. I'm going to look how easy it is to implement them in Edge. It isn't as easy as SVGElement as we don't share the main HTMLAnchorElement base class.
@longsonr you filed the original bug for this in the SVG repo. Are you interested/have time to implement these in Firefox?

Once the mixin is defined (and Firefox supports mixins) I can add an implementation, but you'll need to exclude target from the mixin too as that's an SVGAnimatedString from SVG 1.1. I'm not interested in reimplementing target, just the attributes which are new to SVG 2.

I have a PR for tests for the APIs here that already existed for <a> element in the HTML repo: https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/pull/10275

Firefox already has a patch for all except converting target to return a DOMString. I'm still planning to add these and make the target change in Edge.
@dstorey you mean make `target` no longer an `SVGAnimatedString`? That seems somewhat reasonable to me...

@annevk yeah, we resolved to do that on the SVGWG call as we preferred consistency to HTML than old SVG and there was little compat reason to keep it the way it is: https://www.chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/1109 (it does seem to be growing though, but the number is so small it is probably noise)

General idea seems solid, but a few small issues:

- I think I'd rename your `HTMLHyperlinkElementUtils` into `HTMLOrSVGHyperlinkElementUtils`, and your `HTMLURIReference` into `HTMLHyperlinkElementUtils` (or maybe `HTMLOnlyHyperlinkElementUtils`).
- We'd need to be careful when refactoring the algorithms in what is currently `HTMLHyperlinkElementUtils`, especially as it gets split into two classes. I hope they can all be used, e.g. you can have an "associated url", and all the set the url/reinitialize url/update href algorithms work? It seems like it might be tricky to get them to reflect back into the animVal/baseVal business, but I'm not familiar with that area.
- Can you show `HTMLAreaElement`, or at least its mixins?

> We can ignore animVal as it just mirrors baseVal, so as long as reflecting to baseVal works then we're good to go.

I guess what I'm unsure about, is if the algorithms in HTML say "To update href, set the element's href content attribute's value to X", will that update baseVal/animVal? Or do we need to do something more special?

> HTMLAreaElement is currently:

Right, but it'd be something different after these changes, in order to get `href` back. I guess just include `HTMLURIReference` (or whatever we call it).
HTMLLinkElement has some of this lot too.
I don't think we need to account for HTMLLinkAreaElement here; although it has same-named properties, the logic is not shared in the same way.

I'm not sure you want to share `text` as it's basically a legacy alias for `textContent`, hmm. But otherwise, this is all making sense. Are you interested in working on a pull request so we can iterate further?
